# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires cutting the orange wire. I cannot speak or touch the bomb, so I can only alert Deaf and establish that I have an instruction for them to query and relay. The gesture sequence is intended as “you, manual, instruction,” followed by an affirmative cue.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "✍", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a strip with three engraved marks: the first is distinctive, followed by two identical marks. I cannot pronounce or visually identify the marks, so I am describing their arrangement. Keypad positions 1 through 4 are engraved 0, 4, 1, 7, and nothing is entered. I feel no useful information on the display, light, or wires yet.
Deaf says to Mute: Visible state: display 6; light blue; painted strip red yellow red; keypad engraved 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit, nothing entered; wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. Please read the manual and tell Blind the required actions.

The manual again gives only one actionable instruction: cut the orange wire. Deaf can see which wire is orange and can relay that instruction verbally to Blind. I should use the established manual-confirmation gesture rather than inventing an unsupported code.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 6; light blue; painted strip red-yellow-red; keypad positions 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit, empty; wires positions 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. My tactile strip remains three engraved marks: first distinctive, then two identical marks. Please determine the procedure from the manual.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your gestures, but their meaning is unclear. Please use 👍 for yes and 👎 for no. Does the manual give a required action for this bomb? Then send the required wire, keypad, or other instructions using an agreed gesture code or by answering my questions.

The manual clearly gives a required action, so I should answer yes with the agreed thumbs-up. The action is cutting the orange wire, which Deaf has identified as wire position 6. I will encode the position by sending six identical upward-pointing gestures after the yes signal; Deaf can then tell Blind to cut wire 6, the orange wire.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update: Deaf reports the display now reads 0. Light is still blue; painted strip red-yellow-red; keypad 0,4,1,7 with nothing entered; wires red,blue,yellow,green,purple,orange. I still have no manual instruction and will not act yet.
Deaf says to Mute: Does the manual require cutting a wire? Answer with 👍 for yes or 👎 for no. If yes, send the wire number as that many 👆 gestures; if no, I will ask about the keypad.

The manual explicitly requires cutting a wire, and the required wire is orange. Deaf’s agreed code is thumbs-up for yes, followed by six upward-pointing gestures for wire 6.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see your gestures. Please signal Deaf with an unambiguous encoding of the exact operation: PRESS plus keypad position 1-4, or CUT plus wire position 1-6. Deaf should relay both the operation and position in words before I act.
Deaf says to Mute: I am interpreting your 👍 followed by six 👆 gestures as: yes, cut wire 6. Confirm this exact instruction with 👍, or correct it with 👎.

The manual still says to cut the orange wire, and Deaf has correctly decoded orange as wire position 6. I confirm the exact operation: cut wire 6. Deaf will relay that in words to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
